turns.en: Welcome to episode 455 of the Ractyl Reminder Podcast. I'm Ben Felix, Chief Investment Officer at PWL Capital. And I'm Cameron Passmore, Chief Executive Officer at PWL Capital. And today we are joined by Martin Schmaltz. Martin is a German economist and professor of finance economics and real estate at the University
turns.zh: 欢迎收听 Rational Reminder Podcast 第 435 期。我是 PWL Capital 的首席投资官（CIO）Ben Felix。我是 PWL Capital 的首席执行官（CEO）Cameron Passmore。今天我们请到了 Martin Schmalz。Martin 是一位德国经济学家，目前在 University

turns.en: of Oxford's Said Business School. His research spans asset management, asset pricing, and investor behavior. He is best known for his work on common ownership, which is when one set of shareholders owns competing companies as index fund investors do. We talk about whether index funds for all their benefits carry hidden costs for investors
turns.zh: of Oxford 的 Saïd Business School 担任金融经济学与房地产教授。他的研究横跨资产管理（asset management）、资产定价（asset pricing）和投资者行为。他最为人知的工作是关于共同所有权（common ownership）——也就是同一批股东同时持有互相竞争的公司，指数基金投资者正是这种情况。我们会聊到，指数基金尽管好处多多，但是否给投资者

turns.en: and the broader economy from there, we turn to investor behavior and why wealthy investors often avoid the cheap, diverside portfolios that research supports. We finish on a personal note with why thinking like an economist can make you unhappy.
turns.zh: 和更广义的经济带来了隐性成本。接着我们转向投资者行为，聊聊为什么富裕投资者常常回避研究支持的那种便宜又分散的投资组合。最后我们聊点个人化的话题：为什么像经济学家一样思考，可能会让你不快乐。

turns.en: Well, we'll share our thoughts at the end of the episode, but for now, let's go to our conversation with Martin.
turns.zh: 我们会在节目最后分享自己的想法，现在先进入和 Martin 的对话。

turns.en: Martin Schmaltz, welcome to the Ractyl Reminder Podcast. Thanks very much for having me. We're very excited to be talking to you. Martin, why has index investing grown to its current scale? Mostly because it's an incredibly valuable product offered at a rate of price.
turns.zh: Martin Schmalz，欢迎来到 Rational Reminder Podcast。非常感谢你们邀请我。我们非常期待和你聊。Martin，指数投资（index investing）为什么能增长到今天这个规模？主要是因为这是一个极其有价值、而且价格非常公道的产品。

turns.en: Economists have these theories of how in things are cheap people buy a lot of it. So I think that must be the main reason. So thanks to Jack Bogel, I think the genius of it was not just the product itself, but also how you set up the firm, basically making it a cooperative customer-owned corporation,
turns.zh: 经济学家有一套理论：东西便宜，人们就会买很多。所以我想这一定是主要原因。这要感谢 Jack Bogle，我觉得他天才的地方不只是产品本身，还在于他如何组建这家公司——基本上把它做成了一家合作制的、由客户拥有的公司，

turns.en: which I just conjecture without evidence might be behind them offering the product at cost, as opposed to trying to extract the highest margin out of the value they create. I think we all have to thank him for that. How do you think about how good a deal indexing really is for the individual investor?
turns.zh: 我只能猜测、没有证据，这可能正是他们按成本价提供产品的原因，而不是想从自己创造的价值里榨取最高的利润率。我想我们都得为这一点感谢他。那你怎么看，指数化投资对个人投资者来说到底有多划算？

turns.en: I think your audience is used to that statement, but I mean, it's hundreds of billions of dollars of fee-saved, and not just that, it also just pulled in people into the stock market that otherwise wouldn't have any exposure. If we know anything about the drivers of wealth inequality on earth these days,
turns.zh: 我想你们的听众对这句话已经很熟悉了，但我说的是，这省下了几千亿美元的费用；而且不仅如此，它还把本来完全不会接触股市的人拉进了股市。如果说我们对当今世界财富不平等的驱动因素还有什么认识的话，

turns.en: a lot of it is driven by stock market participation. One would think that it's in an unbelievably good deal for the average individual investor. We're asking about a paper that you have that asks an interesting question about index funds. If index funds are good for each individual investor,
turns.zh: 其中很大一部分就是由股市参与度驱动的。所以人们会认为，对普通个人投资者来说，这是一笔好得难以置信的交易。我们想问你的一篇论文，它对指数基金提出了一个很有意思的问题：如果指数基金对每一个个体投资者都是好的，

turns.en: why is it worth asking whether they're good overall? That's where the heresy starts. Yeah. So you're referring to a paper that started with Bill Zayn at UCLA, and it's titled something like whether indexing is good for investors. And that's like a strange question to ask, given what I just said about how wonderful it is.
turns.zh: 那为什么还值得去问它总体上好不好？异端就从这里开始了。是的。你说的是那篇最初和 UCLA 的 Bill Zame 一起做的论文，标题大概是「指数化投资对投资者是否有利」。考虑到我刚才说它有多美妙，这确实是个奇怪的问题。

turns.en: The question is whether it's good in equilibrium. So it might be good for every individual, but it might have equilibrium effects that are not actually good for each individual investor. We might all be better off without them. That's a theoretical possibility, really out here, that may be clear about this.
turns.zh: 问题在于它在均衡（equilibrium）状态下好不好。所以它可能对每个个体都好，但可能产生一些均衡效应，而这些效应实际上对每个个体投资者并不好。也许没有它们，我们所有人反而过得更好。这只是一种理论上的可能性，我要把这点说清楚。

turns.en: But of course, we could also ask about externalities that indexing could have on other stakeholders, so non-investors, such as consumers, that raises a whole host of issues that traditional finance has just ignored for the last 100 years. How does indexing affect asset prices?
turns.zh: 当然，我们还可以问，指数化投资会不会对其他利益相关者产生外部性（externality），也就是非投资者，比如消费者，这会引出一大堆传统金融学过去 100 年一直忽视的问题。指数化投资如何影响资产价格？

turns.en: So I think there's quite a bit of evidence and simple theory as well that indexing increases as a crisis. The simple model goes, you have a certain amount of supply of equities out there, a certain number of companies with a certain number of sending stock. And if you make holding that stock more attractive,
turns.zh: 我认为已有相当多的证据，也有简单的理论，说明指数化投资会推高资产价格。简单的模型是这样的：市场上有既定数量的股票供给，一定数量的公司、一定数量的流通股。如果你让持有这些股票变得更有吸引力，

turns.en: for example, by making it cheaper to hold the diversified portfolio, that's the whole point of indexing. So you hold supply constant, you increase demand, what happens to price? That's just ECO 101, that the price will go up in financial economics terms, just the risk premium in the market will just go down,
turns.zh: 比如让持有一个分散化组合变得更便宜——这正是指数化的意义所在。那么在供给不变的情况下增加需求，价格会怎样？这就是经济学 101（Econ 101）：价格会上涨。用金融经济学的语言说，就是市场的风险溢价（risk premium）会下降，

turns.en: and you make it cheaper to diversify. Because the individual investors hold less risk. So it stands to reason, and there's a whole bunch of evidence from indexing collusion effects, and so forth, that companies that are captured by the index have lower costs of capital. That's a good side from a corporate finance side.
turns.zh: 而且分散化变得更便宜了，因为个人投资者承担的风险更少了。所以顺理成章地——而且有一大堆关于指数化的合谋效应等等的证据——被纳入指数的公司资本成本更低。从公司金融的角度看，这是好事。

turns.en: But of course, it means for the investor, it has lower expected returns as well. The fun intellectual question that arises is this. So through indexing, you have less risk than if you held individual stocks and were exposed to it as an credit risk. That's a good thing for investor welfare, of course.
turns.zh: 但当然，对投资者来说，这也意味着预期收益更低。由此产生了一个有意思的智力问题：通过指数化投资，你承担的风险比你持有单只股票、暴露在特质风险（idiosyncratic risk）之下要小。这对投资者福利当然是好事。

turns.en: But you also have lower expected returns, which is like a bad thing for investors. And the question is which effect of these and dominates an equilibrium. And this is where at least my intuition runs out, and that's why one needs a model to figure out the answer to that. That's what I've been trying to do with Bill Zayn.
turns.zh: 但你的预期收益也更低，这对投资者来说是坏事。问题就在于，在均衡中这两个效应哪一个占上风。到这一步，至少我的直觉就不够用了，所以才需要一个模型来得出答案。这就是我一直在和 Bill Zame 做的事情。

turns.en: I do want to ask about the model. You mentioned this being heretical. What kind of feedback have you gotten from people when they see this paper? They are honestly upset at the question one asks. Are the weather indexing as good for investors? Again, because I mean, look, we've trained ourselves for a few decades now
turns.zh: 我确实想问问这个模型。你提到这是异端之说。别人看到这篇论文时给了你什么样的反馈？说实话，他们是对我们提出的问题感到不满——「指数化投资对投资者到底好不好」。因为，你看，过去几十年我们已经训练自己去相信——而且是有充分理由地相信——指数化投资对个体是好的。

turns.en: into believing and for good reason that indexing is good for individuals. I'm also not challenging that notion. Everybody who listens and everybody who talks to nothing is change about the fact that if you run across someone who holds a run of individual stocks, not knowing about index funds,
turns.zh: 我也不挑战这个观点。所有听节目的人、所有和我聊过的人，都不会改变这样一个事实：如果你遇到一个持有一堆单只股票、根本不知道有指数基金的人，

turns.en: and it's a good thing for that person to instead hold an index fund and get cheaper diversification. Just nobody has asked the question what the equilibrium effects of that might be and what the welfare effects are. So I think lots of it is really just misunderstanding the question we ask and that there's actually a bit more stuff
turns.zh: 对那个人来说，改成持有指数基金、获得更便宜的分散化，是好事。只是从来没有人问过，这样做的均衡效应和福利效应会是什么。所以我认为很多反应其实只是误解了我们提出的问题，而且这里面更多的东西

turns.en: and not really anything that overturns conventional wisdom, but really just expands on it. Tell us how the model is set up. So there's a few models because we were trying to understand how robust the results are in the simplest version of it. You just think that you have a fixed number of firms,
turns.zh: 并不是要推翻传统智慧，而只是对它做扩展。给我们讲讲这个模型是怎么搭建的。其实有好几个模型，因为我们想弄清楚结果到底有多稳健。在最简单的版本里，你就假设公司数量固定，

turns.en: instead of a fixed number of stockout standing, they have a fixed profit generating process or paid dividends, whatever it might be, all of that is held fixed. So that's the supply of stocks part. And then there is a continuum of investors. So some are more risk-vers than others. Some might be richer than others. Doesn't really matter.
turns.zh: 流通股数量也固定，它们有一个固定的利润生成过程，或者派发固定的股利，诸如此类，这些全都固定不变。这是股票的供给端。然后有一个连续统（continuum）的投资者：有些比其他人更厌恶风险，有些可能比其他人更富，这都无关紧要。

turns.en: And then the key exogenous parameter is just how expensive indexing is. Computers were expensive in 1980. So it was kind of hard to run an index fund. And I think if I remember right from memory, then our index funds went for 76 basis points a year or so. We all know that computers got cheap and then we get the stuff for free now,
turns.zh: 接下来关键的外生参数就是指数化投资有多贵。1980 年时计算机很贵，所以运营一只指数基金挺难的。如果我没记错的话，当时的指数基金收费大约是每年 76 个基点（bps）左右。我们都知道后来计算机变便宜了，于是这些东西现在几乎是免费的，

turns.en: effectively for free anyways. So the question is, then what happens to stock market participation of these investors? And whether they hold individual stocks or the index fund instead, what happens to the asset prices? Just to simplify things, we say, look, these investors, they can only hold a small amount of individual stocks.
turns.zh: 反正实际上是免费的。那么问题来了：这些投资者的股市参与度会发生什么变化？他们是持有单只股票还是转而持有指数基金？资产价格又会怎样？为了简化，我们说，这些投资者只能持有少量的单只股票。

turns.en: So what that would do is just force them to take on interest in credit risk if they wanted any equity exposure at all. And let's hold the index fund, which gets rid of all the interest in credit risk. It's an idealized index fund, like in the textbook, not necessarily like in the real world. But of course they would also hold bonds.
turns.zh: 这样一来，只要他们想有任何股票敞口，就被迫承担特质风险。而如果持有指数基金，就能消除全部特质风险。这是一个理想化的指数基金，像教科书里那样，不一定像现实世界中的那样。当然他们也会持有债券。

turns.en: So the more risk-vers ones are gonna hold a higher fraction of their portfolio in bonds or call that a savings account or a CD, whatever it might be. And the less risk-vers ones are gonna hold a higher fraction in equities. And now as you introduce index funds or just make them cheaper, more people are going to hold an index fund
turns.zh: 所以更厌恶风险的人会把组合中更高的比例放在债券上——你可以叫它储蓄账户或者 CD（大额存单），随便怎么叫。而不那么厌恶风险的人会把更高的比例放在股票上。现在，当你引入指数基金、或者只是让它们变得更便宜时，会有更多人转而持有指数基金，

turns.en: instead of individual equities because the trade-off goes well, for just a small fee, I get a gigantic risk reduction. And others are going to shift more of their bond holdings into equities, the logic being for a small fee, I get a much higher expected return at not that much more of a risk because either some credit risk is taken out.
turns.zh: 而不是持有单只股票，因为这笔账很划算：只付一点点费用，就能获得巨大的风险下降。还有一些人会把更多的债券持仓转成股票，逻辑是：只付一点点费用，就能获得高得多的预期收益，而风险并没有增加太多，因为一部分特质风险被消掉了。

turns.en: None of what I'm saying right now should be surprising to anyone who has thought about these issues. This is a fact that I just described of people taking allocations out of their bond fund or their savings account into the equity market, that's a demand increase. Again, if you buy assumption,
turns.zh: 我现在说的这些，对任何思考过这些问题的人来说都不该感到意外。我刚描述的这个事实——人们把钱从债券基金或储蓄账户挪到股票市场——那就是需求增加。同样，如果你接受这个假设，

turns.en: hold the supply of stocks fixed and increase the demand, it's gotta be true that the stock price goes up. So that is just what happens in the model. The riskiness of the portfolios goes down, but the stock price goes up and it reduces the rate of return. The fun result of this simplified model is,
turns.zh: 保持股票供给不变而增加需求，那么股价必然上涨。所以模型里就是这样的：组合的风险性下降了，但股价上涨，从而压低了回报率。这个简化模型有个好玩的结果：

turns.en: actually every single one of the investors involved, every single one is worse off when you have an index fund or when the index fund gets even cheaper. Then if there was no index fund at all, so everybody likes that the index fund is there and buys it, they act optimally, but in equilibrium it's bad for everyone.
turns.zh: 实际上，参与的每一个投资者，一个都不例外，在存在指数基金、或者指数基金变得更便宜的情况下，反而比根本没有指数基金时过得更差。所以每个人都喜欢指数基金的存在、都去买它，他们的行为都是最优的，但在均衡中这对所有人都是坏事。

turns.en: And the reason is that the risk reduction is precisely reflected in the increase in stock prices. And there's an ex-stomality. The ex-stomality is Ben's acquisitions of stocks, they drive up my stock price, no? The more stocks he buys, the lower my expected rate of return is, as we all know,
turns.zh: 原因在于，风险的下降恰好被股价的上涨所反映。这里有一个外部性。外部性就是：Ben 买股票，会推高我买股票的价格，对吧？他买的股票越多，我的预期回报率就越低，这一点我们都知道。

turns.en: and there's an ex-stomality in a market equilibrium, people do too much of that stuff. So I'm being harmed by Ben's stock market purchases and that's why it can be, again, I'll close this by saying it's a theoretical result. It's a possibility result that the investors actually worse off by the existence of an index fund.
turns.zh: 而在市场均衡中，这类事情存在外部性，人们就会做得过头。所以我被 Ben 的股票购买行为损害了，这就是为什么——我再强调一次，这是一个理论结果，一个可能性结果——投资者可能因为指数基金的存在反而变得更差。

turns.en: And then one can do variations of the model and see, OK, our robustness at result, what I just described, we held the rate of return on bonds constant. What if the supply of bonds is constant and actually, as you shift out from a bond portfolio, the bond prices fall and the yields go up? The yields stay the same and in variations they do,
turns.zh: 然后你可以对模型做各种变体，看看我刚才描述的结果稳不稳健。刚才我们把债券的回报率固定住了。那如果债券供给不变，当你从债券组合中撤出时，债券价格下跌、收益率上升呢？在这些变体里，收益率确实保持不变，我可以细讲，但我已经说了挺久了，所以——

turns.en: I can get into that, but I've been talking for a while here, so. What is the relationship with the fee? Is it a linear relationship where the fee goes down a basis point or is it a different shaped relationship? Good question. I wish I knew a better answer. Notice, look, for these interim results,
turns.zh: 这和费率是什么关系？是线性关系吗——费率每下降一个基点——还是别的形式？好问题，我希望我有更好的答案。注意，对于这些中间结果，

turns.en: we can actually solve that model analytically, but recalling the graphs, it looks kind of linear, but that's not a particularly great answer. OK, interesting. I was just wondering if it's like, if Vanguard Index Fund is three basis points today, does it matter if it goes to two or we basically get the limit of this effect now?
turns.zh: 我们其实可以解析求解，但回想那些图形，看起来差不多是线性的，不过这不是个特别好的答案。好，有意思。我只是在想，如果今天 Vanguard 的指数基金是 3 个基点，那降到 2 个基点还重要吗？还是说我们已经基本触及这个效应的极限了？

turns.en: I think we're probably at the limit of that effect, but that's not a very confident statement. I should be able to go back to that and figure it out. It's really interesting. It's also interesting that the effect in the short term, obviously it is theoretical and who knows where we are in the sort of timeline of the effect playing out,
turns.zh: 我想我们大概已经在这个效应的极限附近了，但这句话说得并不很有底气。我应该回头再算清楚。这真的很有意思。同样有意思的是这个效应在短期内的表现，当然它是理论性的，而且谁知道我们现在处在这个效应展开的时间线上的什么位置，

turns.en: it would appear as if, assuming this theory is a good lens of reality, it would appear that we're at a point where asset prices have gone up, expect the returns have gone down, but from the perspective of everyone participating in the market, unless they're thinking about expected returns, I guess. Everyone's like, wow, this is great.
turns.zh: 但看起来——假设这套理论是观察现实的一个好视角——我们似乎正处在这样一个点上：资产价格已经上去了，预期收益已经下来了，可是从每一个市场参与者的角度看，除非他们真去想预期收益，否则大家都会觉得：哇，太棒了。

turns.en: Returns are really high. Indeed, indeed. And the co-author team, Bill Zamanai, discussed that quite a bit. He's been around for a few decades longer than I have. We have lived that reality ourselves. Now, that's actually something the model can't really speak to because it's a static model,
turns.zh: 收益真的高。确实，确实。我和合著者 Bill Zame 讨论过很多次这一点。他在这个领域的时间比我长几十年。我们自己就活在这个现实里。不过这一点其实是模型说不了的，因为它是一个静态模型，

turns.en: which would be the first critique one could leave it against it, because we live in a dynamic world. So it doesn't really inform these effects across generations, and that's one of the expansions that we're working on to see, whether these welfare effects affect different generations differently and so forth.
turns.zh: 这也可以是人们对它的第一个批评，因为我们生活在一个动态世界里。所以它并不能真正说明跨代之间的这些效应，而这正是我们正在做的扩展之一：看看这些福利效应对不同世代的影响是否不同，等等。

turns.en: The comparison is between two alternative worlds, one in which index hands exists and one in which they didn't. It does not actually speak to the motivation of the fee coming down over the last 40 years and who benefited and who lost, but I mean, the intuition, I certainly share that. This was pretty great for those at Bauder.
turns.zh: 这个比较是在两个替代世界之间进行的：一个有指数基金，一个没有。它其实并没有讨论过去 40 年费率不断下降这个过程本身，也没有说谁受益、谁受损；不过这个直觉我当然认同：这对当年 Bogle 那边的人来说是件大好事。
